card.name: Punctuation ending pregnancy-risk statements
card.fires_on: Punctuation or a space right after a fetal-risk phrase, such as a colon after 'Embryo-Fetal Toxicity' or a period after 'risk to the fetus'. It also fires on the space inside dose units like 'mg/m<< >>2' in animal-study dose lists.

modes.label: After fetus statement
modes.description: The period or colon that closes a pregnancy-risk heading or sentence, just before the next section or advice.
modes.example: Embryo-Fetal Toxicity<<:>> Can cause fetal harm. Advise females

modes.label: Spaces in animal dose lists
modes.description: A space inside or after dose figures in reproduction-study dosing text.
modes.example: (4.5 mg/m<< >>2 ) manifested by increased incidence of various

card.plain: It fires at the punctuation that ends a pregnancy or fetal-harm statement in a drug label, just before the next section starts.
